I split about 2 to 4 hours between really rigorous finger exercises (30 minutes), learning songs (1 hour) - ending with quick chord changes without strumming, just hovering and tapping to build muscle memory.

a minor third sits two frets back and a string down or 3 frets to the right.

major third is increasing the same intervals by one.

on the B string you shift everything one fret.

as long as you know the mode intervals/modes shapes and what scale degree you land on you can play the entire diatonic scale for a key on the fretboard, just visualize the root in different strings and you will never get lost.

chords within "CAGED shapes" are just fuller version of triads, often it repeats the 5th and root on other strings.

if you know how to stack thirds it gets easier to build chords in the spot, you just have to think quick and trust your path.

and account that from the G to B string you shift anything you was doing before by one fret because G to B is a major third opposed by the perfect fourth of other strings.

double bends and sustaining notes is important for phrasing as well, so is repeating notes and alternating the rhythm with how you pick notes.
